messages.subject: more mesh refining?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to refine a mesh to reduce unnecessary computations.
Due to the shape of the area I couldn't find a way with refine arguments or other inla.mesh functions.
The area looks like this.

x <- c(0,0,0,1,1,0.25,0.25,0)
y <- c(0,0.5,1,1,0.5,0.5,0,0)
plot(x,y,type="l")

So the problem is that in the area:
not.need <- cbind(c(0.25,0.25,1,1,0.25),c(0,0.5,0.5,0,0))
lines(not.need,col=3)
...I am getting triangles that are not "all" needed(?).
For instance:
borders=cbind(x,y)
mesh <- inla.mesh.create.helper(points.domain=borders,max.edge=c(0.1,50),offset=c(0.01,0.1))
plot(mesh) ; lines(borders,col=2)

For too fine meshes this is a bit of (computational) problem, eg max.edge=c(0.01,50)
Is it possible to refine this type of meshes to reduce computations for the area that is not of interest?

Thank you in advance.
Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
On 02/09/13 19:53, Alex wrote:
> For instance:
> borders=cbind(x,y)
> mesh <-
> inla.mesh.create.helper(points.domain=borders,max.edge=c(0.1,50),offset=c(0.01,0.1))
> plot(mesh) ; lines(borders,col=2)

points.domain is only helpful for convex domains.  For nonconvex domains
like yours, one can instead specify more precisely what the desired
domain is.  This will give you a sparse extension such that the
triangles are small only inside the specified inner boundary:

borders=cbind(x,y)[nrow(borders):1,] ## Need counterclockwise ordering
mesh <-
inla.mesh.2d(boundary=inla.mesh.segment(borders),max.edge=c(0.1,50),offset=c(0.01,0.1))
plot(mesh) ; lines(borders,col=2)

There are more options available, using inla.nonconvex.hull() to
construct the extension boundary.  Se the third of the SPDE tutorials on
r-inla.org <http://r-inla.org> for an example.

Finn

On 4 September 2013 00:01, Zhao Xing <zhaox...@gmail.com> wrote:
> A: formula = y ~ ClBase4 + CTrt + CBT+ ClAge + CV4 + f(Ind, model="iid") +
> f(rand,model="iid")
> B: formula = y ~ ClBase4 + CTrt + CBT+ ClAge + CV4 + f(Ind,
> model="iid",scale=rep(1,59)) + f(rand,model="iid",scale=rep(1,236))
> C: formula = y ~ ClBase4 + CTrt + CBT+ ClAge + CV4 + f(Ind,
> model="iid",scale=rep(10000,59)) + f(rand,model="iid",scale=rep(10000,236))
> D: formula = y ~ ClBase4 + CTrt + CBT+ ClAge + CV4 + f(Ind,
> model="iid",scale=rep(1,59)) + f(rand,model="iid",scale=rep(10000,236))

You use the default priors for the f()-precision parameters, and they
are the same for all the cases, but the uniform rescaling of the
entire f()-models is effectively equivalent to rescaling the prior
distributions.  I suspect that this explains all the differences in
your results.  In essence, one _shouldn't_ get the same results for
case C and D as for A and B.

I think your original purpose for using "scale" was to treat some
effects as "zero effect"? Then this merely shows that you succeeded
(partly; 10000 isn't large enough to actually give zero effects). A
different approach to that would be to set "Ind" and "rand" to NA for
those entries, as that really means "zero effect" when estimating the
model.  I think "scale" is more appropriate if you have different, but
finite, known scaling factors for each effect.

Not quite; as written in the documentation at
http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/indep.pdf
the scale applies to the precisions, not the variances, so you need to swap the two numbers.
The way you wrote it above, it would be the _precision_ (=1/variance) of X1 that would be twice as big as for X2.

For each of the three cases, there is a specific set of parameters for the tau-prior that gives equivalent models, so for easier interpretability, keep "scale" close to 1 for "standard" effects, and other values around that for "different" effects.

Finn

messages.body_plain:
Dear INLA team,

I have a question about how to combine the SPDE approach with a binomial model of proportion data (# successes and # of trials).

The non-spatial model works fine, where I specify the number of trials using Ntrials in the inla() call – I’ve simplified my variable names to make them more obvious:

nonspatial_formula = NumSucc ~ cov1 + cov2

mod.nonspatial = inla(nonspatial_formula, data = PondData, family = "binomial", Ntrials = NumTrials)

I’ve been trying to specify Ntrials in the INLA call of an SPDE model, with the number of trials included in my data stack:

stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(NumSucc = PondData_e$NumSucc),

  A = list(A.est, 1),

  effects = list(c(ind1, list(Intercept = 1)),

     list(PondData_e[, c("cov1", "cov2", "NumTrials")])), tag = "est")

stack.val = inla.stack(data = list(NumSucc = NA),

  A = list(A.val, 1),

  effects = list(c(ind1, list(Intercept = 1)),

    list(PondData_v[, c("cov1", "cov2", "NumTrials")])), tag = "val")

stack.two = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.val)

formula_spatial = NumSucc ~ -1 + Intercept + cov1 + cov2 + f(i, model = spde)

spde1 = inla.spde2.matern(m2, alpha = 2)

data_propwet = inla.stack.data(stack.two, spde = spde1)

result_propwet = inla(formula_spatial,

      data = data_propwet,

      family = "binomial",

      Ntrials = data_propwet$NumTrials,

      control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack.two), compute = TRUE),

      control.compute = list(dic = TRUE)

      )

The error I get is:

Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :

  arguments imply differing number of rows: 20045, 35655

My data have 20045 rows; 35655 is the number in the stack after NAs are added. The bigger number comes from the Ntrials piece (if I mess with it and say, for example, Ntrials = data_propwet$NumTrials[15000:16000], then the second number becomes however many rows I’ve specified there).

Because I don’t fully understand the stack functionality, I want to be sure I don’t specify the wrong rows for the weights, since that would make my analysis nonsensical.

One potential solution is to specify the number of trials outside the stack by doing:

Ntrials = c(PondData_e$NumTrials, PondData_v$NumTrials)

The model does run this way, but I want to be sure that I’m not making the data line up in the wrong way. Is this correct?

Also, I have one other question:

I have spatiotemporal data and I have been comparing a model with a separable spatial and AR1 structure (i.e. f(i, model = spde) + f(i.group, model = "ar1")) with a spatial model with lagged covariates which make biological sense (so the second model doesn’t have an AR1 component). A.est = inla.spde.make.A(m2, loc = as.matrix(PondData_e[, c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y")]), group = PondData_e$Yr_group, n.group = n_years)

A.val = inla.spde.make.A(m2, loc = as.matrix(PondData_v[, c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y")]), group = PondData_v$Yr_group, n.group = n_years)

ind1 = inla.spde.make.index(name = 'i', n.spde = m2$n, n.group = n_years)

Is this ok to retain in the model without the AR1 piece, or should I create A without the groups?

Thank you for all the work you have put into creating this program, and thanks in advance for taking the time to answer my questions.

Helen

The Ntrials information should go in the data list, not the effects

list, in the inla.stack calls,
i.e. the first line of the first inla.stack() call should be
stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(NumSucc = PondData_e$NumSucc,
Ntrials=PondData_e$NumTrials),
and in the inla() call you should then use
    Ntrials= data_propwet$Ntrials

> Because I don’t fully understand the stack functionality, I want to be sure
> I don’t specify the wrong rows for the weights, since that would make my
> analysis nonsensical.

There is an example using inla.stack and Ntrials in Section 3.1 of
this tutorial:
http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/spde-tutorial-from-jss

> Ntrials = c(PondData_e$NumTrials, PondData_v$NumTrials)
>
> The model does run this way, but I want to be sure that I’m not making the
> data line up in the wrong way. Is this correct?

In this case, yes, this should give you the right thing, but the other
way described keeps everything together in the stacks, making it
easier to use only one of the stacks when calling inla(), for example.

> I have spatiotemporal data and I have been comparing a model with a
> separable spatial and AR1 structure (i.e. f(i, model = spde) + f(i.group,
> model = "ar1")) with a spatial model with lagged covariates which make
> biological sense (so the second model doesn’t have an AR1 component). In all
> the models, I’ve been setting up A as though I will run the AR1 structure
> (here Yr_group is 1 for the first year of data, and so on):

The A matrix you use in the model that doesn't use a group/AR1 model
must be setup with n.group=1.
If the alternative model is simply independent replicates for each
year instead of AR1, then you need to replace "group" with "repl" in
the inla.spde.make.A() call, and specify f(..., replicates=i.repl)
instead of f(group=i.group) in the formula.

For example, the A.est of the AR1 model,

> A.est = inla.spde.make.A(m2, loc = as.matrix(PondData_e[, c("POINT_X",
> "POINT_Y")]), group = PondData_e$Yr_group, n.group = n_years)

turns into this for independent replicates:

A.est = inla.spde.make.A(m2, loc = as.matrix(PondData_e[, c("POINT_X",

"POINT_Y")]), repl = PondData_e$Yr_group, n.repl = n_years)

If the alternative model is based on a single replicate of the spatial
effect then you need both n.repl=1 and n.group=1.

In essence, the number of columns in the A-matrix must be equal to
n.spde*n.repl*n.group, where the n.* values match whatever you specify
in the f()-formula and in inla.spde.make.index().

Finn

messages.subject: Nested random effects
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to figure out how to specify nested random effects in INLA and would also like to estimate the variance components of such effects.  I have started by trying to implement some of the simple examples from Pinheiro and Bates.  I have two questions:

1) When I calculate the standard dev attributable to a random effect (using inla.contrib.sd <http://inla.contrib.sd>()) the estimates are similar to those from lme when the Maximum Likelihood method is used, and are shrunk relative to an lme fit with REML.  Is it possible to obtain estimates from an inla fit that are more in line with those produced by using REML in lme?

2) How can nested random effects be specified?

The code below illustrates these questions.

Thanks,

Julin

library(INLA)
library(nlme)
data(Machines)
?Machines #3 machines, each tested by 6 workers.

m <- as.data.frame(Machines) #so that we have the same format going into lme and inla
head(m)

lme1 <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker,data=m)
summary(lme1)

inla1 <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid"),data=m)
summary(inla1)
inla.contrib.sd <http://inla.contrib.sd>(inla1)$hyper
#INLA and lme similar but sd estimates for the random effects are smaller from INLA.
   #Why?  INLA estimates are similar to Maximum Likelihood estimates in lme:

lme1b <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker,data=m,method="ML")
VarCorr(lme1b)

##What about a nested model?  We nest Machine inside of Worker to estimate the
   #variance of workers on different machines
lme2 <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker/Machine,data=m,method="ML")
summary(lme2)
VarCorr(lme2)

#unsure how to do this in INLA
#separate random effects don't work:
inla2 <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid") + f(Machine,model="iid"),data=m)
summary(inla2)
inla.contrib.sd <http://inla.contrib.sd>(inla2)$hyper

##Could make a new term that represents the machine.worker combo
m$machine.worker <- paste(m$Machine,m$Worker,sep=".")
inla2b <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid") + f(machine.worker,model="iid"),data=m)
summary(inla2b)
inla.contrib.sd <http://inla.contrib.sd>(inla2b)$hyper
VarCorr(lme2) #lme has  larger variance for Machine than inla

##note that lme4 can handle this type of specfication
detach("package:nlme")
library(lme4)

lmer2 <- lmer(score ~ Machine + (1|Worker) + (1|machine.worker),data=m,REML=F)
summary(lmer2)
